strapline: A sharper public foundry for high-signal repositories, workflow systems, and operator-grade open-source infrastructure.
description: Repo Foundry is a magazine-style discovery site for repositories worth studying, shipping against, or borrowing ideas from across AI, automation, coding agents, media systems, and practical developer workflows.
publicBoundary: The public site shows only curated, public-safe research records. Internal session notes, local paths, repo telemetry, and manager-only backlog data stay out of the public build.

news.title: open-webui/open-webui released v0.9.1
news.summary: open-webui/open-webui published v0.9.1. Highlights include 🐛 Missing aiosqlite dependency. Fixed a startup crash (ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'aiosqlite') when installing Open WebUI via pip or uv by adding the missing aiosqlite package to pyproject.toml. The dependency was listed in requirements.txt but not in the published package metadata, so it was not installed automatically. 23916; 🐛 Missing asyncpg dependency. Added the missing asyncpg package to pyproject.toml to prevent the same startup crash for PostgreSQL users. Like aiosqlite, it was present in requirements.txt but absent from the published package dependencies..
highlights: 🐛 Missing aiosqlite dependency. Fixed a startup crash (ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'aiosqlite') when installing Open WebUI via pip or uv by adding the missing aiosqlite package to pyproject.toml. The dependency was listed in requirements.txt but not in the published package metadata, so it was not installed automatically. 23916

🐛 Missing asyncpg dependency. Added the missing asyncpg package to pyproject.toml to prevent the same startup crash for PostgreSQL users. Like aiosqlite, it was present in requirements.txt but absent from the published package dependencies.

editorialNotes.title: How we curate
editorialNotes.body: We bias towards repos with real traction, real momentum, and a believable path to practical reuse. The goal is not to hoard links. It is to surface work we can actually learn from, build against, or operationalise.

editorialNotes.title: What we care about
editorialNotes.body: The strongest signals here sit around AI control planes, workflow automation, creator infrastructure, developer productivity, and the open-source systems shaping modern coding-agent work.

editorialNotes.title: Why the public feed is curated
editorialNotes.body: The public site is intentionally lighter than the internal manager view. It keeps the useful research, readable summaries, and public-safe structure while leaving out workspace operations, private notes, and live internal coordination.
